package.title: Open Weightと非US Model Family — Qwen・DeepSeek・Kimi・Mistral・GLM
package.editorial_angle: gpt-ossをopen-weight deploymentのanchorにし、Qwen、DeepSeek、Kimi、Mistral、GLMをreasoning/coding/tool use、deployment、service lifecycleの差で比較する。国・企業ランキングではなく技術スタックの選択肢拡大として読む。
must_cover: open weightsとtraining/data transparencyを混同しない
Alibaba Model Studioのsnapshot/regional/global availabilityをupstream release dateに統合しない
DeepSeek API service transitionとcheckpoint publicationを分離
boundaries: Open weights do not imply an unrestricted data/training disclosure; openness should be described specifically in terms of weights/license and deployment.

The Model Studio page is a living deployment catalog; it mixes release, snapshot, regional availability, and later global availability entries. Architecture must not collapse those into one upstream model release date.
These dates establish DeepSeek API service transitions; upstream training/checkpoint publication dates must not be inferred when not stated.

The hash-pinned Kimi Code 'What's New' page is a living product document whose current rendered history begins much later; item chronology was cross-checked against Kimi's first-party platform blog/changelog during interactive verification.
The news index reliably establishes publication chronology and titles; detailed benchmark/license claims require item-level pages and should remain vendor-attributed if used in drafting.
Performance superlatives in the release notes are vendor claims; use only release identity, dates, stated feature scope, and clearly attributed evaluation claims.

runner.invocation: Interactive ChatGPT evidence review of hash-pinned Special Evidence package plus preserved first-party Source Intake snapshots; item-level first-party pages were followed where living indexes required pagination/navigation; no paid inference-provider API.

grouping_resolution.note: Release announcement and model card are one open-weight package.

sources.title: Primary source 1: https://api-docs.deepseek.com/updates/
sources.role: Primary source used for chronology and technical verification

claims.text: DeepSeek's API changelog records V3.1 on August 21, V3.1-Terminus on September 22, V3.2-Exp on September 29, and V3.2 on December 1.
The changelog maps deepseek-chat and deepseek-reasoner to non-thinking and thinking modes of these model versions.
V3.2-Speciale was exposed through a temporary endpoint with no tool calls and an explicit expiration, so it is not equivalent to the stable V3.2 service.

limitations.text: These dates establish DeepSeek API service transitions; upstream training/checkpoint publication dates must not be inferred when not stated.
